result.title: Early-Pregnancy Calcium and Protein Intake Are Associated with Newborn Bone Mineral Density in Women with Obesity.
result.abstractText:
Background

Maternal vitamin D status, calcium, and protein intake during pregnancy may influence offspring bone health. However, these associations are poorly understood in females with obesity, who are often advised to restrict dietary intake.

Objectives

To examine associations between maternal vitamin D status, calcium and protein intake in early and late pregnancy, and newborn areal bone mineral density (aBMD) among females with obesity.

Methods

In the treatment of obese pregnant women study, 231 offspring underwent dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry scans within 48 h after birth to assess aBMD. Analyses included 218 and 208 mother-newborn dyads with dietary data and 175 and 171 dyads with maternal vitamin D data in early and late pregnancy, respectively.
